newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EDMONTON IN FIRST TIE IN CLUB'S HISTORY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-EDMONTON IN FIRST TIE IN CLUB'S HISTORY.

text.p: Curtis Joseph made 52 saves, including 21 in the third period, as the Edmonton Oilers played the first scoreless tie in franchise history, battling to a 0-0 deadlock with the Detroit Red Wings on Tuesday.
Joseph posted his fourth shutout of the season, tying him with Detroit's Chris Osgood for second in the NHL. Osgood stopped 21 shots for his 12th career shutout.
This was the third scoreless deadlock in the NHL this season.

At the Islanders, Niklas Andersson had two goals and three assists, including four points in a six-goal second period, as the New York Islanders throttled the Phoenix Coyotes, 8-2 for their third straight home win.
The five points were a career high for Andersson, who had nine in his first 24 games this season.
Marty McInnis, Bryan Berard, Zigmund Palffy and Bryan Smolinski each added a goal and two assists for the Islanders.

In Philadelphia, Eric Desjardins and John LeClair scored second-period goals and Eric Lindros added a key insurance tally as the Philadelphia Flyers stretched their unbeaten streak to a season-high five games with a 5-4 victory over the Florida Panthers.
Joel Otto and Scott Daniels also scored for the Flyers.
The Flyers carried a 4-1 lead into the third period and it stayed that way until rookie Jason Podollan's power-play goal with 8:28 remaining made it 4-2.

Just 45 seconds later, Lindros converted a breakaway into his second goal of the season and a 5-2 lead, but Martin Straka drew the Panthers within two 26 seconds later with his second goal of the season.
In Toronto, Denis Pederson, Brian Rolston and Bill Guerin each had a goal and an assist as the New Jersey Devils recorded their first win of the decade in Toronto, defeating the Maple Leafs, 5-2.

After the teams swapped goals in the first period, Pederson and Guerin tallied 2:23 apart in the second to open a 3-1 advantage. Martin Brodeur made the lead stand up with 25 saves to improve to 12-7-1.
In Calgary, Jonas Hoglund's goal with 49 seconds left in regulation lifted the Calgary Flames into a 5-5 tie with the Ottawa Senators in a battle of struggling teams.

The Flames, winless in five straight and nine of their last 10 games, pulled goaltender Dwayne Roloson for an extra attacker with just over a minute remaining. Cory Stillman passed the puck to Corey Millen, who sent it to Hoglund, who one-timed a wrist shot through goaltender Damian Rhodes' pads for the equaliser.

In Los Angeles, red-hot Jaromir Jagr scored his league-leading 28th and 29th goals as the Pittsburgh Penguins extended their unbeaten streak to eight games with a 5-3 victory over the Kings, their first win in Los Angeles in more than eight years.
Jagr has 14 goals during a nine-game goal-scoring streak. He also extended his points streak to 11 games.
Mario Lemieux added a goal and an assist and Petr Nedved and Dave Roche also scored for the Penguins.
